source: Original Okok.jpg from user-uploaded Okok.jpg.zip. Each of the 17 marker locations is aligned to its individually labeled user-supplied Quizlet screenshot; cyan line/circle overlays only. Origin-region prompts remain explicit for femoral and sciatic nerves.

models.name: Cervical nerves

questions.question: Which spinal nerve group is marked in the neck?

models.reference: User supplied individual Cervical nerves screenshot; marker aligned to vertical neck region.

models.name: Cervical plexus

questions.question: Which plexus is formed mainly by C1–C4 in the marked upper-neck region?
questions.explanation: Cervical plexus. Its usual core is C1–C4; the supplied course list calls it C1–C5. The phrenic nerve receives C3–C5 contributions.

models.reference: User supplied individual cervical plexus screenshot; shorter vertical marker on upper neck left of cervical nerves marker.

models.name: Brachial plexus (C5–T1)

questions.question: Which plexus is marked at the base of the neck and shoulder?
questions.explanation: Brachial plexus, formed from C5–T1 ventral rami.

models.reference: User supplied individual brachial plexus screenshot; diagonal line at base of neck.

models.name: Thoracic nerves (T1–T12)

questions.question: Which spinal nerve group is marked along the ribs?
questions.explanation: Thoracic spinal nerves are T1–T12. Most continue as intercostal nerves; T12 is subcostal.

models.reference: User supplied individual thoracic nerves screenshot; long line to image-right of spine across rib cage.

models.name: Phrenic nerve

questions.question: Which nerve is marked on the side of the neck?
questions.explanation: Phrenic nerve (C3–C5), supplying the diaphragm. Neck marker follows the supplied Quizlet reference.

models.reference: User supplied individual phrenic nerve screenshot; short vertical marker on image-right side of neck.

models.name: Axillary nerve

questions.question: Which nerve is indicated by the circled shoulder region?
questions.explanation: Axillary nerve, a branch of the brachial plexus supplying the deltoid and teres minor.

models.reference: User supplied individual axillary nerve screenshot; circle over image-left shoulder.

models.name: Ulnar nerve

questions.question: Which nerve is indicated by the arrow in this elbow close-up?
questions.explanation: Ulnar nerve passes behind the medial epicondyle and continues toward the little-finger side of the hand.

models.reference: User supplied individual ulnar nerve screenshot; circle near image-left elbow. Precise arrow targets the individual nerve within that reference region; nearest-neighbor close-up for distinction.

models.name: Median nerve

questions.question: Which nerve is indicated by the arrow in this elbow close-up?
questions.explanation: Median nerve runs along the anterior forearm and enters the hand through the carpal tunnel.

models.reference: User supplied individual median nerve screenshot; matched circle near image-left elbow. Precise arrow targets the individual nerve within that reference region; nearest-neighbor close-up for distinction.

models.name: Radial nerve

questions.question: Which nerve is indicated by the arrow in this elbow close-up?
questions.explanation: Radial nerve supplies the posterior compartments of the arm and forearm.

models.reference: User supplied individual radial nerve screenshot; matched circle near image-left elbow. Precise arrow targets the individual nerve within that reference region; nearest-neighbor close-up for distinction.

models.name: Lumbar nerves (L1–L5)

questions.question: Which spinal nerve group is marked in the lower back above the sacrum?

models.reference: User supplied individual lumbar nerves screenshot; short vertical marker below rib cage beside lumbar spine.

models.name: Sacral nerves (S1–S5)

questions.question: Which spinal nerve group is marked at the sacral region?

models.reference: User supplied individual sacral nerves screenshot; vertical marker in sacral region below lumbar nerves.

models.name: Lumbar plexus (L1–L4)

questions.question: Which plexus is marked lateral to the lumbar spinal nerves?
questions.explanation: Lumbar plexus, chiefly L1–L4, gives rise to the femoral nerve.

models.reference: User supplied individual lumbar plexus screenshot; short line immediately image-left of lumbar spine.

models.name: Sacral plexus (L4–S4)

questions.question: Which plexus is marked in the pelvic region?
questions.explanation: Sacral plexus, L4–S4, gives rise to the sciatic nerve.

models.reference: User supplied individual sacral plexus screenshot; short vertical line immediately image-left of sacral spine.

models.name: Femoral nerve

questions.question: Which nerve is indicated by the circle near its lumbar plexus origin?
typedAnswers: femoral nerve starts from lumbar plexus
questions.explanation: Femoral nerve arises from the lumbar plexus (L2–L4). The circle follows the supplied reference near its origin.

models.reference: User supplied individual femoral nerve screenshot; circle near lumbar plexus origin.

models.name: Sciatic nerve

questions.question: Which nerve is indicated by the circle near its sacral plexus origin?
typedAnswers: sciatic nerve starts from sacral plexus
questions.explanation: Sciatic nerve arises from the sacral plexus (L4–S3) and descends through the posterior thigh.

models.reference: User supplied individual sciatic nerve screenshot; circle at image-right pelvic region near sacral plexus origin.

models.name: Tibial nerve

questions.question: Which nerve is indicated by the circled region below the knee?
questions.explanation: Tibial nerve continues through the posterior leg toward the plantar foot.

models.reference: User supplied individual tibial nerve screenshot; circle at image-right upper calf just below knee.

models.name: Common fibular nerve

questions.question: Which nerve is indicated by the circled region near the lateral knee?
questions.explanation: Common fibular (common peroneal) nerve runs toward the fibular head before dividing.

models.reference: User supplied individual common fibular nerve screenshot; circle at lateral image-left knee.
